items.title: Send these readings to your care team this week
items.text: 14.9% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL (weeks 11-12); the usual target is under 5%. Your average was 211.5 mg/dL. Contact your care team this week rather than waiting for your next visit.

rejected.text: Your average blood sugar was 211.5 mg/dL, and 14.9% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL, so contact your care team this week. Your care team can help you get your blood sugar back on track.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal went with a smaller rise in blood sugar, about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in real adults and 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the synthetic program. Walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner got most of the gain, with a rise 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Only 16.7% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, which is good because sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Keep having dinner before 8 pm to avoid a bigger rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 8.2 hours, and you never reached 13 hours of fasting. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points in the randomized program, but it's not clear if this applies to you.
